claims.claim: Tomcat's default pool is 200 platform threads, and each waiting request holds one thread, so each pod stopped accepting at about 200 waiting requests
claims.about: Spring Boot on Tomcat with platform threads (java-spring)
claims.measured: java-spring I/O wait (10 ms, 256 connections): 15,611 req/s, p50 15.01 ms, p99 29.52 ms, 491 MB
claims.why: The benchmark doesn't test how many requests can wait at once or a 30-second hold, so the 200-thread ceiling can't be checked against it.

claims.claim: With spring.threads.virtual.enabled, waiting requests park cheap virtual threads
claims.measured: java-spring-vt I/O wait (256 connections): 14,571 req/s, p99 37.37 ms, 444 MB, compared with 15,611 req/s and 491 MB for platform threads
claims.why: The I/O-wait test used only 256 connections with 10 ms waits, so it can't show what virtual threads cost per parked request at thousands of long waits; at that small scale they weren't faster or much smaller.

claims.claim: With virtual threads and max-connections 12000, the gateway should hold 10,000 waiting connections per pod
claims.about: Spring Boot with virtual threads on Tomcat (java-spring-vt)
claims.why: No test went above 256 connections or held requests for 30 seconds, so a capacity of 10,000 connections per pod can't be checked.
